properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 3:55AM EDT until October 11 at 7:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Avery County in western North Carolina...
Northwestern Burke County in western North Carolina...
West Central Caldwell County in western North Carolina...

* Until 700 AM EDT.

* At 355 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated new rounds of heavy rainfall
are approaching northern Burke, western Caldwell, and southeastern
Avery County. Between 4 and 6 inches of rain have fallen over the
past 12 hours with an additional 1-2 inches of rainfall possible.
Several streams remain above Minor Flood Stage, including the
Wilson Creek and the Johns River. Flash flooding is ongoing and new
areas of flash flooding may develop within the next 1-3 hours.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat- access
areas, and campgrounds.  Significant flooding of
poor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.
Low-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring
barricades.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Morganton, Longview, Valdese, Salem, Icard, Drexel, Hildebran,
Connelly Springs, Rutherford College and Glen Alpine.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

The additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and
debris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in
the past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly
at the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a
landslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a
sudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to
investigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or
getting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.

properties.areaDesc: Caldwell, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 3:52AM EDT until October 11 at 9:45AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Caldwell County in western North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 945 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible. A
few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible. A small
culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 339 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a round of moderate
rainfall recently has departed eastern Caldwell County, with
additional cells of moderate rainfall moving into the county from
the south.  This rainfall is occurring on top of saturated soils
resulting from a prolonged period of light to moderate showers
that occurred over the county yesterday. Storm-total rainfall of
2.5 to 4.5 inches has been observed across eastern Caldwell
County since yesterday, with the highest totals from Cajah's
Mountain to Sawmills and Granite Falls.  Areas streams have been
steadily rising in response to this heavy rainfall and isolated,
out-of-bank conditions impacting low-lying areas adjacent to
streams are likely to develop over the next 1-3 hours.

Areas of greatest concern include along Lower Creek in Lenoir,
where a streamgauge on Harrisburg Dr is at 8.53 feet and
approaching the Action/Advisory Stage of 9.0 feet. At 9.0 feet,
flooding of low-lying, undeveloped woodland surrounding Lenoir
Mall will begin.

- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms may develop
through 9am this morning.  These showers and storms will be very
efficient at producing heavy rainfall.  Soils are saturated and
streams are swollen. Therefore, additional heavy rain may quickly
create new areas of flooding and cause previous areas of flooding
to redevelop.  As a result, a Flash Flood Warning may be issued
this morning.  Caution is advised near any stream or other
vulnerable area.  Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain
develops.  Please have a plan in place should flash flooding
develop and do not hesitate to act.  Please heed all evacuation
orders from Emergency Management officials.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Hickory, Lenoir, Sawmills, Granite Falls, Gamewell, Hudson,
Cajah's Mountain, Rhodhiss, and Cedar Rock.

- Https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 11 at 3:37AM EDT until October 11 at 1:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Kent.

* WHEN...From 7 AM this morning to 1 PM EDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.areaDesc: Mobile Coastal; Baldwin Coastal; Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 11 at 2:30AM CDT until October 11 at 6:00PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH THIS AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Joshua Tree NP West; Joshua Tree NP East; Chiriaco Summit
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 11 at 12:27AM PDT until October 11 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southern California, including the following
areas, Chiriaco Summit, Joshua Tree NP East and Joshua Tree NP
West.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel will continue to bring
moderate to heavy rainfall at times this morning before tapering
off this afternoon. Localized rainfall rates of one to two inches
per hour will be possible at times, which may lead to localized
flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Duluth MN to Port Wing WI
properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 11 at 2:23AM CDT until October 11 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Duluth MN
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisory, southwest winds 10 to 20
kt with gusts up to 30 kt and waves 1 to 2 ft. For the Gale
Watch, northeast winds 20 to 25 kt with gusts up to 35 kt and
waves 4 to 7 ft possible.

* WHERE...Duluth MN to Port Wing WI.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 7 AM CDT this
morning. For the Gale Watch, from late tonight through Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds can cause hazardous waves which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should consider altering plans to avoid possible
hazardous conditions.  Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter
course, and/or secure the vessel for severe wind and waves.
